items.title: Miri’s landslide-prone roads on Canada Hill set for RM30 million rebuild in 2027
items.summary: “At the moment, we cannot determine what method will ultimately be used to improve the affected sections, including whether the road foundation needs to be reconstructed and the road widened, or whether a bridge structure needs to be built at certain sections. He said should landslides recur after the repairs, the affected sections would have to be dealt with again, underscoring the need for a professional engineering design. However, Lee stressed that immediate action would still be taken to address dangerous sections while awaiting implementation of the RM30 million reconstruction project.

items.title: Fake cop, real loss: Ipoh man conned of RM1.9m in phone scam
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 6 — An elderly man lost RM1.9 million to a phone scam after he was contacted by a suspect impersonating a police officer. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the victim, 78, lodged a police report Friday, claiming he had been intimidated by the fake police officer who convinced him that he was involved in an investigation. He also reminded the public that the police would never instruct anyone to transfer money into certain accounts for investigation purposes.

items.title: US Navy musician wins Sabah hearts with 'Original Sabahan' rendition
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A US Navy musician has captured Sabahans' hearts after her rendition of the popular local song 'Original Sabahan' at the launch of Pacific Partnership 2026 (PP26) here two days ago went viral. US Navy Musician 3rd Class Jasmine Rodriguez, 29, said her colleagues had described 'Original Sabahan' as Malaysia's version of 'Country Roads' because it was familiar to every generation and easy to sing along to. "It's one of those songs that everyone knows and everyone can sing along to," she told the New Straits Times during the Pacific Partnership Band performance at a shopping mall here last night.

items.title: Police probe alleged mistreatment of two-year-old girl at Temerloh nursery after viral video
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 6 — Police are investigating a case involving a two-year-old girl who was allegedly mistreated by a babysitter at a nursery in Temerloh. Temerloh police chief ACP Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the girl’s 29-year-old mother lodged a report at around 6 pm yesterday. A video clip showing the child allegedly being mistreated by the nursery caretaker has also gone viral on social media, sparking widespread public reaction.

items.title: Bintulu schools go online till Sept 11 as haze pushes API past 200
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 6 — A total of 54 primary schools and nine secondary schools in Bintulu Division, comprising the Bintulu and Tatau/Sebauh districts, will be closed from Sept 7 to 11 due to haze, with Home-Based Teaching and Learning (PdPR) to be implemented during the closure. “The temporary closure of 54 primary schools involving 22,476 students and nine secondary schools involving 17,268 students under the Bintulu and Tatau/Sebauh PPDs (District Education Offices) will be from Sept 7 to 11, 2026,” the statement said. Overall, 617 primary schools involving 130,953 students and 93 secondary schools involving 107,350 students under 14 PPDs affected by the cross-border haze in Sarawak have been temporarily closed.

items.title: Beneath the surface, peat fires keep burning
items.summary: This is among the challenges facing firefighters as the Fire and Rescue Department prepares for the possibility of severe fires flaring up in the country's forests should the current hot and dry spell persist. Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad, said peat fires are particularly difficult to control because they spread beneath the surface and take considerably longer to extinguish than conventional bush fires. The department is closely monitoring 62 locations nationwide, identified as being prone to large-scale forest fires exceeding 25ha.

items.title: US Embassy denies seeking to influence Malaysia's political leadership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The United States Embassy in Kuala Lumpur has denied ever seeking to determine Malaysia's political leadership, calling any suggestion otherwise false. In a statement, United States Chargé d'Affaires David H. Gamble Jr said Washington had never sought to decide Malaysia's political leadership. The statement follows speculation online over the United States' alleged role in Malaysia's domestic political affairs.

items.title: Police probe alleged mistreatment of 2-year-old at Temerloh nursery
items.summary: KUANTAN: Police are investigating the alleged mistreatment of a two-year-old girl by a nursery caretaker in Temerloh. Temerloh police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the girl's 29-year-old mother lodged a report about 6pm yesterday. He said the completed investigation paper would be referred to the public prosecutor for further instructions.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD seeks landmark state victory as Saxony-Anhalt votes
items.summary: BERLIN, (Germany): Voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt will go to the polls on Sunday in a closely watched election that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to take power at a state level since the World War Two. Under the smiling 35-year-old leader Ulrich Siegmund, the party has been polling comfortably ahead for months, and there is a genuine chance the AfD could take an absolute majority on Sunday evening, particularly if several smaller parties fail to clear Germany's five per cent threshold to enter parliament. Weeks of coalition talks could follow Sunday's vote.

items.title: Argentina threatens to sanction oil projects around Falklands
items.summary: BUENOS AIRES: Argentina has announced that it will investigate and sanction oil companies working near the Falkland Islands without authorisation, after President Javier Milei said the "winds of change" favour his country's claim to the archipelago. Britain and Argentina fought a 10-week war in 1982 over the South Atlantic islands, a British overseas territory that Argentines call Las Malvinas. According to Argentine media, they include British, US, Canadian, Israeli, Danish and Dutch companies.

items.title: Century-old Penang coffee shop to close [WATCH]
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 106-year-old Hainanese coffee shop will close on Sept 26 as no family member is willing to carry its three-generation legacy into the future. "Nowadays, youngsters don't tend to do business like a coffee shop. Tan himself never intended to take over the family business.

items.title: Ronald Stephen McCoy: Enduring legacy of courage, compassion and hope
items.summary: DATUK Dr Ronald Stephen McCoy, the renowned Malaysian obstetrician and gynaecologist, physician, humanitarian and lifelong campaigner for nuclear disarmament, passed away on Sept 1, 2026 at the age of 96. In 1987, he founded the Malaysian Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War, linking Malaysian doctors to the international movement against nuclear weapons. He suggested the name International Campaign to Abolish Nuclear Weapons (ICAN).

items.title: Two dead, 14 missing after Bolivia army base blasts
items.summary: VIACHA, (Bolivia): At least 14 soldiers remained missing after two explosions at a military base in Bolivia killed two and injured more than 80, the base commander said Saturday. The blasts occurred Friday afternoon at a facility where explosives are stored in the town of Viacha, home to about 114,000 people and located 30 kilometres (18 miles) southwest of La Paz. "Fourteen uniformed personnel who were in the area affected by the two explosions at the Viacha military base have not yet been located," base commander Colonel Antonio Amaru said in a statement, adding that search and rescue efforts were underway.

items.title: Tens of thousands of Croatians protest over hazardous waste
items.summary: ZAGREB: Tens of thousands of people rallied in Zagreb on Saturday seeking the immediate cleanup of thousands of tonnes of illegally dumped hazardous waste in one of Croatia's most pristine areas. Some 35,000 tonnes of waste, including electronic and medical waste, were found in early 2025 in the Lika region, known for its pristine forests and rivers and home to national parks and the country's longest mountain range. They are suspected of importing waste from Slovenia, Italy and Germany and illegally dumping or burying it alongside medical waste from Croatia in Gospic, in the pristine region.

items.title: Putin holds Ukraine talks with US envoys
items.summary: MOSCOW: Russian leader Vladimir Putin held around three hours of late-night talks in the Kremlin with US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff on ending more than four years of war with Ukraine on Saturday, ahead of their first visit to Kyiv on Sunday. Talks ended after just over three hours, past 11pm in Moscow. Putin said Russia would ensure the safety of the envoys in Kyiv — a city Moscow has pounded with deadly strikes throughout the war.

items.title: Negligence is all it takes to spark huge fire, warns Fire Dept
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A carelessly discarded cigarette butt, an unattended pile of burning rubbish or a small fire used to clear land is all it takes to ignite a major bush or peat fire during the current hot and dry spell. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad said prolonged dry weather had stripped moisture from grass, bushes and other vegetation, effectively providing ready fuel for fires. [[nid:1526600]] Nor Hisham said strong winds could spread flames through dry vegetation, widening the area firefighters must contain.

items.title: Negligence is all it takes to spark huge fire, warns Fire Dept
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A carelessly discarded cigarette butt, an unattended pile of burning rubbish or a small fire used to clear land could be all it takes to ignite a major bush or peat fire during the current hot and dry spell. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad said prolonged dry weather had stripped moisture from grass, bushes and other vegetation, effectively providing ready fuel for fires. [[nid:1526526]] Nor Hisham said strong winds could make the situation worse by rapidly carrying flames across dry vegetation and expanding the area firefighters have to contain.

items.title: US, Iranian forces fire at vessels in waters near Iran
items.summary: DUBAI: US and Iranian forces fired at vessels in waters around Iran on Saturday, including three Iranian oil carriers struck by the Americans and three tankers that Iran said it targeted while on unauthorised routes in the Strait of Hormuz. US Central Command said it struck the three Iranian vessels, including one off the coast of Kharg Island, near Iran's oil export hub, after Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched ballistic missiles at two US Navy ships. The IRGC responded by threatening intensified strikes against US military vessels in the region, and said later it targeted the three tankers as well as three US-linked vessels in other areas.

items.title: Beneath the surface, peat fires keep burning
items.summary: This is among the challenges facing firefighters as the Fire and Rescue Department prepares for the possibility of severe fires flaring up in the country's forests should the current hot and dry spell persist. Its director-general, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohamad, said peat fires are particularly difficult to control because they spread beneath the surface and take considerably longer to extinguish than conventional bush fires. The department is closely monitoring 62 locations nationwide, identified as being prone to large-scale forest fires exceeding 25ha.

The department is closely monitoring 62 locations nationwide, identified as being prone to large-scale forest fires exceeding 25ha.

items.title: History must inspire, not remain a ‘silent witness’, says National Archives chief as Malaysia marks 69 years of independence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 6 — As Malaysia commemorates 69 years of Merdeka, the National Archives of Malaysia (ANM) said history must be more than a record of the past, serving instead as a source of inspiration and lessons for Malaysians to understand how the nation was built. “Although ANM has a substantial collection of official records, we also collect records from private organisations, NGOs and individuals, as well as conduct oral history interviews. — Picture by Firdaus Latif In the context of Merdeka, Zaidin said ANM currently holds about 30,000 archival files — roughly 200,000 pages of documents — related to the Malayan Union alone.

items.title: Venezuelan billionaire once probed by US now has Pentagon oil deal
items.summary: CARACAS/MIAMI: The billionaire who helped broker the Trump administration's sweeping long-term oil deal with Venezuela was until recently a target of US money-laundering investigations involving funds embezzled from the state-owned oil company PDVSA. Now, after assisting US authorities ahead of the capture of authoritarian leader Nicolas Maduro, Alejandro Betancourt is Washington's key partner in an unusual oil agreement with Caracas. According to last week's announcement, the US gains access to about one-fifth of Venezuela's crude reserves for decades.

items.title: Malaysia's Taanusiya Chetty wins second runner-up at Miss World 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Teacher and activist Taanusiya Chetty has been crowned the second runner-up at the 2026 Miss World pageant, which was held in Vietnam today. The iconic sapphire-studded crown went to Joheirry Mola of the Dominican Republic, who was crowned Miss World this year. A total of 111 contestants from around the world took part in the pageant, which was held in Nha Trang.

items.title: Dismantle the corruption 'gravy train' to end systemic corruption
items.summary: Its significance extends beyond the individual corruption cases currently before the courts. Corruption becomes particularly dangerous when access to public office, public resources and political influence creates opportunities for private enrichment. By the time a corruption case reaches court, public money may already have been lost, institutions damaged and public confidence weakened.

items.title: Haze shuts 63 schools in Bintulu, Tatau and Sebauh
items.summary: KUCHING: A total of 63 schools in Bintulu, Tatau and Sebauh will be closed from Sept 7 to 11 after the air pollutant index (API) reading in Bintulu reached the "very unhealthy" level. The Sarawak Education Department (JPNS) said the temporary closure involved 54 primary schools with 22,476 students and nine secondary schools with 17,268 students under the Bintulu and Tatau/Sebauh District Education Offices (PPDs). With the latest closures, a total of 617 primary schools involving 130,953 students and 93 secondary schools involving 107,350 students under 14 PPDs affected by cross-border haze in Sarawak have been temporarily closed.

items.title: NST Leader: Were 'foxes' in charge of Tabung Haji?
items.summary: TABUNG HAJI is cash-rich, but as the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) found out, it was governance-poor. Little wonder then that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is supporting tighter oversight of Tabung Haji, saying the measure is necessary to prevent abuse of power and other irregularities in the fund's management. Tighter oversight plus legal support have been long overdue.

items.title: Haze forces last-minute cancellation of PJ Half Marathon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Petaling Jaya Half Marathon, which was expected to draw 10,000 participants tomorrow, has been cancelled due to the haze. In a post on the PJ Half Marathon's Facebook page about two hours ago, the organisers said the decision was made after taking into consideration the Air Pollutant Index readings, as well as the health and well-being of the runners. Petaling Jaya Mayor Datuk Mohd Yazid Sairi had said last month that the event would also feature international runners from 34 countries.

items.title: Grief on Chinese Internet as wait for Tibet flood news drags on
items.summary: PHOTOS of sons, daughters, uncles and husbands pepper Chinese social media, shared by people hoping for news about relatives missing since deadly floods on the border with Nepal on Aug 26. In neighbouring Nepal, authorities have given regular updates on the rising number of dead and display names of the missing, while national media show images of families grieving. Chinese official media has neither shared the names of the missing nor published much footage of the families' reactions.

items.title: Rayer calls for probe into alleged Pas-US meeting
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Jelutong member of parliament RSN Rayer has called for an investigation into an alleged meeting between Pas leaders and United States officials concerning efforts to topple the government. Rayer said the allegation, reportedly revealed by Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang at the party's muktamar, could not be dismissed as a political anecdote. It is a matter of national security and national sovereignty," he said tonight.

items.title: One year after founder's death, Armani needs to find a new fit
items.summary: ONE year after the death of founder Giorgio Armani, the Italian fashion house is entering a pivotal period as the clock starts ticking on plans for an initial stake sale, after the group spent the last year focused on governance. Over the last year, Armani's sales declined 2.8 per cent at constant currencies to €2.2 billion, and investors remain cautious about the luxury sector's health as the war with Iran drags on and Chinese consumer spending falters. He said Armani was still in a transition phase and looking for a new balance as the founding family worked closely with new board directors, including former Gucci CEO Marco Bizzarri.

items.title: Man suffers head, leg injuries after falling from tree
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A 45-year-old man sustained head injuries and a fractured leg after falling from a tree while picking fruit at Gunung Berembun here this afternoon. A Negri Sembilan Fire and Rescue Department spokesman said the department received an emergency call at 2.49pm. "Additional assistance from the Special Tactical Operation and Rescue Team was required as the victim was seriously injured after falling from a tree," the spokesman said.

items.title: Jom Heboh gives Melaka businesses an economic boost
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The Jom Heboh concert in Melaka is more than an entertainment event, with its large crowds helping to drive the local economy and benefiting small businesses and entrepreneurs. "I want every celebration we create to bring benefits back to the people," he said when speaking at the Jom Heboh Concert held in conjunction with the Karnival Anak Muda Melaka x Konsert Jom Heboh at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here tonight. Meanwhile, the two-day Karnival Anak Muda Melaka, which began yesterday, has attracted about 50,000 visitors.

items.title: Sultanah Aminah Hospital launches probe into sexual harassment allegations involving specialist
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) has launched an internal investigation into allegations of sexual harassment involving a medical specialist in the Department of Anaesthesiology. The Johor Health Department, in a statement today, said the hospital management had established a special investigation committee to investigate the report, which was received on Aug 28. It said the investigation followed a report by a portal alleging that certain parties had asked the complainant to withdraw the misconduct report concerning the sexual harassment allegations.

items.title: Jokowi calls on leaders, people to build peace through mutual understanding
items.summary: Opening the Penang Peace Dialogue alongside Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow here tonight, Jokowi said leaders must understand and respond to the concerns and aspirations of their people. However, he said responsibility for building peace did not rest with leaders alone, as the people must also understand the direction and challenges faced by their leaders. Jokowi said a strong society was not one that merely made demands, but one that also understood the direction and challenges faced by its leaders.

items.title: After the muktamar, Pas faces the harder part [WATCH]
items.summary: KOTA BARU: After four days of speeches, resolutions and political messaging, the 72nd Pas Muktamar has ended. It also provided an indication of how Pas wants to position itself for the political battles ahead. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the resolutions reflected the party's response to current issues affecting the people and the country.

items.title: Final victim found, four‑day search ends in Kota Tinggi drowning tragedy
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 5 — The last victim, Mohamad Haiman Fitri Supian, who was reported missing in a drowning incident at Pantai Tanjung Lompat, Kota Tinggi, was found at 3.05pm today. Acting Tanjung Sedili Maritime Zone director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the victim’s body was found by the public about 3.1 nautical miles from the incident location. Mohd Najib said the discovery ended the four-day search and rescue (SAR) operation coordinated by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA).

items.title: ‘Round‑the‑clock service’: Puspakom plans 24‑hour operations for vehicle inspections
items.summary: KLANG, Sept 5 — The Computerised Vehicle Inspection Centre (Puspakom) plans to extend its operating hours to 24 hours a day starting next January to provide greater convenience to the public for vehicle inspections. Puspakom Chief Executive Officer Mahmood Razak Bahman said the implementation would depend on public response to the extension of operating hours to seven days a week from November, as well as the availability of sufficient manpower. Meanwhile, Mahmood said Puspakom was introducing several other innovations, including a new “community hero” recognition award and an expansion of on-site inspection services for customers.

items.title: Miti seeks Budget 2027 allocations to accelerate semiconductor industry, expand Malaysian exports
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has submitted 11 initiatives to the Finance Ministry (MOF) for consideration in Budget 2027, which will be tabled next month. Deputy Miti Minister Sim Tze Tzin said priority would be given to efforts to accelerate the semiconductor industry as a high-growth, high-value sector capable of creating more jobs for Malaysians. Sim, who is also Bayan Baru member of parliament, said Miti had also proposed allocations to help Malaysian companies, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises, penetrate new and previously underexplored overseas markets.

items.title: Sarawak haze crisis prompts nationwide plea to stop open burning, shield schools and businesses
items.summary: SARIKEI, Sept 5 — All parties are urged to refrain from open burning activities to prevent the haze situation in Sarawak from worsening and posing risks to public health and daily activities. Special Select Committee on Infrastructure, Transportation and Communication chairman Datuk Yusuf Abd Wahab said all open burning activities, including the disposal of rubbish and clearing of forests through fire, must cease until the situation returns to normal. Put these activities on hold until the haze situation improves.

items.title: Ops Vulture arrests two in Teluk Intan, police seize five ATM cards, gold jewellery
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — Police arrested two men yesterday over unlicensed money-lending and possession of ATM cards belonging to others, during an operation codenamed Ops Vulture in Teluk Intan. Hilir Perak police chief ACP Chua Kok Lian said the suspects were arrested by the district’s Commercial Crime Investigation Division. Two ATM cards belonging to other people and RM300 cash were found on him.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching says Meta must extend Facebook, Instagram safeguards worldwide for under‑18s
items.summary: Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the safety features should not be limited to users in the United States, as young people in other countries, including Malaysia, also face the risk of internet addiction. She said the measures are in line with the government’s direction to ensure that young people, particularly those under 16, do not use social media excessively. Teo said measures to protect young people must be implemented comprehensively by all social media platforms and not just Meta.

items.title: Budget 2027 plan: Fadhlina pushes Kasih Madani training expansion to protect children nationwide
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Sept 5 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek will propose including the Kasih Madani home childminder training programme in Budget 2027 to provide greater childcare and safety support for working mothers. Fadhlina, who is also the Nibong Tebal MP, said expanding the initiative would allow more childminders to receive formal training, improve childcare quality, and strengthen the home childcare ecosystem. Sharing her personal experience, Fadhlina revealed that three of her children were cared for by home childminders, and her second child was subjected to physical abuse by a childminder.

items.title: Emergency remains: Uggah says Serian still under haze alert despite API improvement
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Serian remains under the haze emergency despite its Air Pollutant Index (API) reading improving from the hazardous level, with the Sarawak Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) continuing to closely monitor the situation. SDMC chairman Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas said in a statement today that the Serian air quality monitoring station recorded an API reading of 334 as at 10am, placing the area in the hazardous category. Uggah said the monitoring would be carried out before any recommendation was made to the Sarawak Premier and Prime Minister regarding the status of the emergency in Serian.

items.title: Melaka to study proposal to set basic salary at RM2,500-RM2,800, says CM
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 5 — The Melaka government will study a proposal to make the state one of the earliest in Malaysia to set a basic salary of between RM2,500 and RM2,800 before submitting its recommendation to the Federal Government. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said the proposal would be assessed from all angles before being submitted to the Federal Government. He said the state government would also create opportunities for women who had left their careers due to various factors, particularly through new projects being developed in the state.

items.title: Malaysia may see 230 million tonnes of plastic waste by 2040, with 23 million entering waterways yearly, says ministry
items.summary: Deputy secretary-general (Environmental Sustainability) Datuk Nor Yahati Awang pointed out that approximately 23 million tonnes of this plastic waste are discharged into waterways annually, representing a significant threat to marine ecosystems. In response, she said NRES has formulated a range of strategies and initiatives to enhance marine waste management nationwide, including the development of a uniform monitoring framework through coastal clean-up programmes. “These efforts include beach clean-ups, systematic data collection, and monitoring.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms and heavy rain in eight states until 6pm
items.summary: MetMalaysia said in a statement that the weather conditions were expected in Kedah, Penang, Perak, Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang, Sarawak and Sabah. The affected areas are Bandar Baharu and Kulim in Kedah, Seberang Perai Selatan, Seberang Perai Tengah and Seberang Perai Utara (Penang), and Kinta, Kampar, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang and Kuala Kangsar (Perak). The warning also covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai and Jeli (Kelantan), Besut (Terengganu) and Cameron Highlands (Pahang).

items.title: Abdul Karim: Kuching gears up for Malaysia Day celebration expected to draw 5,000
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Approximately 5,000 people are expected to gather at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) for the Malaysia Day celebration on September 16. He added that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg are also expected to attend the official ceremony, scheduled to begin at 8.15 pm. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, who is this year’s Malaysia Day celebration co-chairman, will attend the meeting online.

items.title: Haze affects tourist arrivals and upcoming events in Sarawak, says state minister
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Sarawak has seen a slight drop in tourist arrivals amid the current haze, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. He said the decline was expected to continue until the haze situation improved. Abdul Karim said tourists planning to visit Sarawak might change their travel plans due to the haze.

items.title: MACC detains company owner for allegedly soliciting RM30,000 to secure defence‑sector financing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Kuala Lumpur has arrested an owner of a consulting, management and business company on suspicion of soliciting and accepting bribes of about RM30,000 in return for obtaining grants and loans under the Bumiputera entrepreneur financial financing scheme for two companies related to armaments and defence. According to sources, the woman, in her 60s, was arrested at about 6.45pm on Thursday around Kuala Lumpur. Meanwhile, Kuala Lumpur MACC director Mohamad Zakkuan Talib when contacted confirmed the arrest and the case is being investigated under Section 16(a) (A) of the MACC Act 2009.

items.title: Serian tops very unhealthy API readings as six Sarawak areas exceed 200
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — A total of six areas in Sarawak recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at very unhealthy levels as of 1pm today with Serian recording the highest reading of 287. Deputy Director-General (Development) of the Department of Environment (DOE) Azuri Azizah Saedon said five other areas in the state that recorded very unhealthy readings were Kuching (267), Sri Aman (251), Samarahan (242), Samalaju (202) and Bintulu (201). She said 25 areas recorded API readings at unhealthy levels involving Negeri Sembilan, Melaka, Johor, Pahang, Sabah, Labuan, Sarawak and Selangor, in addition to 26 areas recording moderate air quality status and 11 areas at good levels.

items.title: In Nepal for eight days, Malaysian wife presses on with search for missing special‑operations firefighter
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Hani Othman, who has been in Nepal for eight days to follow the developments in the search for her missing Special Airborne Fire and Rescue Team (PASKUB) officer husband, today joined a mission to distribute humanitarian aid to disaster victims in the country, while hoping to find any clues as to her husband. Hani, who is currently on her way from Nuwakot to Betrawati with the local non-governmental organisations (NGO) Samundra Nepal NGO and Himalayan Leaders, said that the area they are heading to is not the last location where her husband’s vehicle was detected, but she still hopes that the journey will yield clues. “The area of my husband’s last point is further up.

items.title: Malaysia sends families’ DNA samples to Nepal to help identify 55 missing Malaysians, says Tok Mat
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 5 — All DNA samples from the next-of-kin of 55 Malaysians still unaccounted for following floods and landslides in Nepal have been obtained, said Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan. He said the samples would be sent to Nepal for the authorities there to conduct DNA matching, a process expected to take some time given the large number of victims involved. Mohamad said Malaysia was also prepared to send experts from the Department of Chemistry to assist the Nepalese authorities with the DNA matching process, if required.

items.title: Chew Jetty heritage site unaffected by blaze, Penang govt to help owners of five destroyed premises, says CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 5 — The historic Chew Jetty here was unaffected by a fire that broke out about 20 metres away and destroyed five business premises early this morning, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the state government was ready to provide assistance to the owners of the five business premises, including support for rebuilding efforts. Chow said the Penang Fire and Rescue Department, assisted by the Volunteer Fire Brigade, had brought the fire under control, while efforts to remove the timber stacks continued after traces of the fire were detected in the wooden structures.

items.title: ‘If Langkawi too small’: Defence minister says LIMA may need alternative venue
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 5 — The proposal to explore an alternative venue for the Langkawi International Maritime and Aerospace Exhibition (LIMA) in the future is aimed at keeping the event competitive amid growing competition among defence exhibitions in the region. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said continuous improvements to LIMA, particularly in terms of venue size and facilities, were necessary, especially as more neighbouring countries were also organising similar exhibitions. Mohamed Khaled said the government should consider developments in the defence exhibition industry in neighbouring countries, which now offer more extensive facilities and exhibition space.

items.title: Government ready to declare emergency if API exceeds 400, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA BERANG, Sept 5 — The government is ready to propose declaring an emergency for any area that records an Air Pollution Index (API) reading of more than 400, in line with the standard operating procedure for haze management in the country. Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the measure could be considered if the API reading was at a very dangerous level, as happened in Serian, Sarawak which recorded a reading of more than 500, leading to the declaration of an emergency. Arthur said so far only three of the 68 API monitoring stations nationwide had recorded very unhealthy readings, namely in Kuching, Samarahan and Sri Aman in Sarawak, while Serian recorded readings at a dangerous level.

items.title: ‘Not just Kota Kinabalu’: MOH targets Sandakan, Tawau clusters in Sabah specialist expansion
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 5 — The Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) will begin placing resident specialists in several hospitals in Sabah such as Kota Marudu and Beaufort as a measure to overcome the shortage of specialists in the state. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the effort also complements the ministry’s initiative to move specialist rotation to rural areas in Sabah. Dr Dzulkefly said MOH has also aggressively expanded the Hospital Services Outsourcing Programme initiative to the private sector to address congestion in public hospital lobbies and wards.

items.title: Serian town unusually quiet amid thick haze and emergency declaration
items.summary: SERIAN, Sept 5 — The usually vibrant streets of Serian town, typically bustling with weekend crowds, appeared unusually quiet today, amidst the ongoing haze and the declaration of an emergency in the area. A Bernama check around the town found that health concerns had disrupted daily activities. However, the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings on the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed a downward trend from the hazardous levels above 500 recorded the day before.

items.title: Thai DPM Sihasak to undertake two‑day working visit to Malaysia from Sept 6
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 5 — Thailand’s Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Sihasak Phuangketkeow, is scheduled to pay a two-day working visit to Malaysia from Sunday to September 7, according to the PR Thai Government. In its Facebook post on Friday, it noted that the visit would follow up on and advance the issues discussed by the leaders of the two countries during the Thai Prime Minister’s official visit to Malaysia on July 9 to 10. The delegation is scheduled to meet Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan to discuss border security and joint development of border areas.

items.title: Zambry: Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026-2035 aims to shape students with strong values alongside academic excellence
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 5 — The Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026–2035 is focused on developing students who are not only academically competent but also grounded in strong values and good character. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the goal of education is not merely to produce knowledgeable and skilled graduates, but to shape better individuals who are capable of navigating a changing world and the demands of the job market. “The purpose of education is to make us better people.

items.title: Workplaces in Serian may operate during haze emergency with health precautions, says SDMC
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 5 — Government, private offices and other workplaces affected by the haze emergency in Serian, including industries, plantations, construction sites and quarries may continue their operations but must take health precautionary measures. Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, who is also state Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) chairman, said the committee is closely monitoring the haze situation across Sarawak, particularly the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in Serian. “SDMC is currently monitoring the API level in Serian within these three days in anticipation for any fluctuation of the API level, should it increase to a level above 500.
